summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman was admitted for worsening bilateral lower extremity edema and cellulitis, with a history of chronic lymphedema, morbid obesity, and recurrent infections. She presented with increased swelling, erythema, and mild shortness of breath, and was found to have leukocytosis and stable renal function. Treatment included a 10-day course of IV clindamycin for cellulitis, IV diuresis with furosemide that was later transitioned to oral bumetanide, and management of a supratherapeutic INR due to antibiotic interaction by temporarily holding warfarin and initiating a heparin drip. Her infection resolved, INR stabilized, and she was discharged home on her baseline medications, including warfarin and bumetanide, with instructions to complete a course of fluconazole for oral thrush and follow up for lab monitoring. Despite aggressive diuresis, weight reduction was minimal due to the challenges of fluid management in severe lymphedema.
problems: Morbid (severe) obesity due to excess calories
Epilepsy, unspecified, not intractable, without status epilepticus
Personal history of malignant neoplasm of other organs and systems
Personal history of other venous thrombosis and embolism
Family history of ischemic heart disease and other diseases of the circulatory system
